pred_reasoning_trace: A 32-year-old woman presented with a 1-year history of slow but progressive swelling near her gluteal cleft. She denied fevers, chills, pain, drainage, bleeding, or rectal bleeding. On examination, there was a 4 × 4 cm area of swelling just left of the natal cleft at the level of the tip of the coccyx, with mild blanching erythema of the overlying skin but no fluctuance, purulence, or visible pilonidal pits. Given a high suspicion for abscess, percutaneous aspiration was performed in clinic but no fluid was obtained. The differential diagnosis at this time included inclusion cyst and soft-tissue tumor. The patient was scheduled for surgical excision. In the operating room, a 6-cm vertical incision was made over the lesion in the prone jack-knife position. A complex and septated 6 × 4 × 4 cm mass was excised from the subcutaneous tissue near the coccyx, with a rim of healthy tissue; the mass was adherent to subcutaneous fat but did not involve the coccyx or anal sphincter. The specimen was oriented with sutures and sent for permanent pathology, and the wound was closed primarily.
